title: Consumer protection has visible routing but unresolved recovery, remedy, and trust gaps
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of Federal Reserve household fraud respondents, FTC reports, CFPB published complaints, and student-loan complaint timing fields

observations.period: 2024; Federal Reserve SHED household fraud and recovery

denominator.unit: weighted adult population estimate; loss/recovery measures condition on adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

non_credit_card_fraud_lost_money.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

non_credit_card_fraud_some_money_not_rec.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud

spent_ten_or_more_hours_recovering.unit: percent of adults experiencing non-credit-card fraud, approximate

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2024 SHED weighted estimates; exposure, conditional loss, recovery, and time cost are retained as separate endpoints.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported survey estimates concern the most recent relevant incident and do not establish verified fraud, complete incidence, event-level recovery, causal firm responsibility, or remedy adequacy.
observations.subgroup: All adults, with non-credit-card fraud loss/recovery conditional on the relevant fraud experience; age-conditioned incidence and loss are separate universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Credit-card liability protections may limit direct loss; reported recovery and time cost can reflect reporting, recall, scam type, assets, or access to help rather than a uniform consumer-protection failure.

denominator.unit: approximate consumer fraud reports received by FTC

imposter_reported_losses.unit: US dollars reported lost, more than

investment_scam_reported_losses.unit: US dollars reported lost, more than

observations.method: FTC administrative totals and 2020-2025 comparison reported in Joint Economic Committee testimony; approximate and lower-bound language is retained.
observations.uncertainty: Reports are unverified, may include multiple contributors and changing reporting access, and undercount unreported fraud. Reported losses are not a complete loss census or recovery measure.
observations.subgroup: All FTC consumer-fraud reports, with imposter and investment categories retained separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher reported losses can reflect reporting propensity, category mix, high-value cases, or coverage changes; administrative visibility is not household prevalence or remedy success.

denominator.unit: published CFPB complaint records in 2020; 2025 has 5,452,107 records

observations.method: Official CFPB API annual aggregation of published complaints; response labels, narratives, and monetary/non-monetary categories are administrative publication endpoints, not verified household outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error; published-record selection, product mix, routing, coding, index timing, and the 2025 in-progress category may drive changes. Complaint records do not provide account denominators or representative consumer exposure.
observations.subgroup: All published complaints pooled across products and years in this comparison; product-conditioned layers remain separate.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower monetary-relief label may reflect coding, product mix, routing, or publication change rather than lower remedy; an explanation label is not necessarily adequate correction or trust repair.

denominator.unit: published student-loan complaint records in 2024; 2025 has 21,333 records

observations.method: Official CFPB product-filtered API aggregation and annual-report comparison; the company_response field and separate timely field are preserved as different administrative endpoints.
observations.uncertainty: No sampling standard error or elapsed-days measure; year-over-year movement may reflect servicing, routing, publication, coding, taxonomy, or index changes. No borrower harm, payment interruption, or verified remedy is observed.
observations.subgroup: Student-loan complaints in the CFPB published product-filtered data.
observations.counterinterpretation: The field divergence is not a contradiction and cannot be read as a uniform deterioration in servicing without case-level notices, transfer dates, payment status, elapsed time, and remedy records.

related_sources.claim: SHED supplies household exposure, conditional loss, recovery, and time-cost estimates.
FTC supplies administrative reported-loss and category scale context.
CFPB supplies the published complaint-response trend.
CFPB student-loan audit preserves separate timing fields and their interpretation boundary.

boundary: This is a non-pooled consumer-power bridge from reported exposure and loss through administrative visibility and response labels toward recovery and trust. It does not establish representative prevalence, verified firm liability, remedy adequacy, account-level exposure, switching, exit, trust repair, or political action. A lawful same-case or linked household/account ledger remains required for those arrows.
